title: Dial plans
blurb: Enterprise dial plans, +E.164 patterns, Unified CM normalization, and the simulator's teaching order.

lessons.title: Dial plans, patterns, and routing choices
lessons.summary: A Webex Calling dial plan is enterprise-wide. It lists patterns and one routing choice, which is a trunk or a route group.

paragraphs: The trunk article says dial plans are configured globally for the enterprise and apply to all users, regardless of location.

lessons.title: Unified CM normalization toward the cloud
lessons.summary: The workflow guide normalizes Unified CM callers to +E.164, then uses one partition of route patterns toward the local gateway for Webex Calling DID ranges.
objectives: Explain why one pattern set is enough
Keep this on the cluster, not on the phone

diagram.caption: Habits become +E.164 on Unified CM. One route list points at the gateway.

flow.title: A Unified CM phone calls a Webex Calling DID

steps.label: Dial a habit
steps.detail: Translation patterns or inbound transformations produce +E.164.

steps.label: Match the DID range
steps.detail: A partition representing Webex Calling destinations holds a +E.164 route pattern per DID range.

steps.label: One member
steps.detail: The route group that contains the SIP trunk to the local gateway.
steps.inspect: No extra members in the guide's description

steps.label: Deliver
steps.detail: The cloud rings the Webex Calling user.
steps.inspect: Return path is the cloud dial plan

paragraphs: Because every habit becomes +E.164, the guide says one set of route patterns is enough, independent of how the user dialed.
Skipping normalization means a pattern per habit, and they drift.

cite.label: Webex Calling configuration workflow

sections.h: PSTN calls are a different pattern
paragraphs: The same cluster still sends true PSTN out its own gateway or, if you chose premises PSTN for Webex users, via the local gateway from the cloud side.
Do not point every pattern at Webex Calling. Only the ranges that live there.

lessons.title: What this lab will not call a dial plan
lessons.summary: Outgoing permissions, call queues, and emergency routing are adjacent. They are not dial-plan patterns. Mixing them hides the real object.
lessons.uncertainty: Calling permissions exist in the product. This lesson does not invent the current permission names. Check Control Hub and the calling feature docs for the control you will actually set.
objectives: Keep 911 out of the ordinary pattern list
Keep queues out of the dial plan

diagram.caption: Permissions, features, and emergency sit beside the dial plan.

steps.label: Block international
steps.detail: That is a calling permission, documented with the user and location calling settings. Confirm the current control in Control Hub.
steps.inspect: Do not fake it with a pattern that drops the call

steps.label: Send a range to the PBX
steps.detail: That is a dial plan.

steps.label: Answer with a menu
steps.detail: That is an auto attendant.

steps.label: Route 911
steps.detail: That is emergency calling for the location.
steps.inspect: Not a pattern of last resort

paragraphs: A user who cannot dial internationally may still match a dial plan when they dial a local PSTN number. Fix the permission, not the pattern.
An auto attendant number is a feature with a number. It can also be a target of dialing. Building the menu is not a pattern edit.

lessons.title: Pattern misses
lessons.summary: A miss is not automatically a failure. On premises PSTN it is fallthrough to the local gateway. On a cloud connection it is cloud PSTN, unless the origin rule blocks it.
objectives: Add a pattern when fallthrough is the wrong trunk

diagram.caption: No pattern. The location's PSTN connection decides the rest.

steps.label: No match
steps.detail: Say so explicitly in the ticket.

steps.label: Fallthrough
steps.detail: The workflow guide sends unknown destinations to the local gateway.
steps.inspect: That may be the right PRI or the wrong one

steps.label: Cloud PSTN
steps.detail: Fine for a Webex user and a real public number.
steps.inspect: Not fine for a private extension

steps.label: Stop
steps.detail: Cloud PSTN will not take the call.

paragraphs: An on-prem extension that is not a Webex Calling destination will fall through. If the location trunk is a PSTN carrier, the carrier will reject a private extension.
That is the bug the dial-plan object exists to prevent.

cite.label: Trunks, route groups, and dial plans

paragraphs: Even when fallthrough would reach the right gateway, a pattern documents the range.
The next admin can see it. Fallthrough is invisible.
